# Flow (pressure drop)

## `calculate_pressure_drop`

Multiphase pressure gradient at one point in a pipe using a chosen correlation. Returns gradient components, holdup, flow regime and hydraulics.

**Price:** Costs 1 credit.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.calculate_pressure_drop) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#calculate_pressure_drop) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.calculate_pressure_drop)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number | yes | Pipe angle from vertical in degrees, in the flow direction (0=vertical upflow, 90=horizontal, 180=vertical downflow) |
| `correlation` | string | yes | Multiphase flow correlation (e.g. "Beggs-Brill", "Griffith-Wallis", "KISS"). One of `Aziz`, `Baxendell-Thomas`, `Beggs-Brill`, `CHAOS`, `Dukler`, `Duns-Ros`, `Fancher-Brown`, `GOAT`, `Gray`, `Griffith-Wallis`, `Hagedorn-Slug`, `KISS` and 9 more. |
| `density` | array of number | yes | Densities [gas, oil, water] in kg/m3 |
| `diameter` | number | yes | Pipe diameter in meters |
| `ift` | number | yes | Gas-liquid interfacial tension in N/m |
| `pressure` | number | yes | Pressure in MPa |
| `roughness` | number | yes | Absolute pipe roughness in meters |
| `velocity` | array of number | yes | Superficial velocities [gas, oil, water] in m/s |
| `viscosity` | array of number | yes | Viscosities [gas, oil, water] in Pa.s |

### Example: horizontal Beggs-Brill

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.calculate_pressure_drop(
        angle=90.0,
        correlation="Beggs-Brill",
        density=[100.0, 850.0, 1000.0],
        diameter=0.1,
        ift=0.03,
        pressure=10.0,
        roughness=0.0001,
        velocity=[2.0, 1.0, 0.0],
        viscosity=[1e-05, 0.001, 0.001],
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { GraphSolve } from "@graphsolve/sdk";

    const gs = new GraphSolve();
    const response = await gs.calculate_pressure_drop({
        "angle": 90.0,
        "correlation": "Beggs-Brill",
        "density": [100.0, 850.0, 1000.0],
        "diameter": 0.1,
        "ift": 0.03,
        "pressure": 10.0,
        "roughness": 0.0001,
        "velocity": [2.0, 1.0, 0.0],
        "viscosity": [1e-05, 0.001, 0.001]
    });
    console.log(response.result);
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    use graphsolve::GraphSolve;
    use serde_json::json;

    let gs = GraphSolve::new()?;
    let response = gs
        .call("calculate_pressure_drop", &json!({
            "angle": 90.0,
            "correlation": "Beggs-Brill",
            "density": [100.0, 850.0, 1000.0],
            "diameter": 0.1,
            "ift": 0.03,
            "pressure": 10.0,
            "roughness": 0.0001,
            "velocity": [2.0, 1.0, 0.0],
            "viscosity": [1e-05, 0.001, 0.001]
        }))
        .await?;
    println!("{:?}", response.result);
    ```

## `compare_pressure_drop_correlations`

Run every multiphase pressure-drop correlation (or a subset) on one segment and compare the predicted gradients.

**Price:** Costs 3 credits.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.compare_pressure_drop_correlations) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#compare_pressure_drop_correlations) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.compare_pressure_drop_correlations)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number | yes | Pipe angle from vertical in degrees, in the flow direction (0=vertical upflow, 90=horizontal, 180=vertical downflow) |
| `correlations` | array | no | Optional subset of correlations. Default: every correlation. |
| `density` | array of number | yes | Densities [gas, oil, water] in kg/m3 |
| `diameter` | number | yes | Pipe diameter in meters |
| `ift` | number | yes | Gas-liquid interfacial tension in N/m |
| `pressure` | number | yes | Pressure in MPa |
| `roughness` | number | yes | Absolute pipe roughness in meters |
| `velocity` | array of number | yes | Superficial velocities [gas, oil, water] in m/s |
| `viscosity` | array of number | yes | Viscosities [gas, oil, water] in Pa.s |

### Example: all correlations

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.compare_pressure_drop_correlations(
        angle=90.0,
        density=[100.0, 850.0, 1000.0],
        diameter=0.1,
        ift=0.03,
        pressure=10.0,
        roughness=0.0001,
        velocity=[2.0, 1.0, 0.0],
        viscosity=[1e-05, 0.001, 0.001],
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```
